problems.title: A quadratic without real roots
problems.question: Find the sum of roots of $3x^2-7x+5=0$ from the listed choices.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: $D=b^2-4ac$; Vieta’s sum is $-b/a$ when both roots are included over the complex numbers.
steps: The discriminant is $49-60=-11$, so there are no real roots to sum in the school real-number setting.
Over the complex numbers the two roots have sum $7/3$, also absent from the numerical choices.
problems.answer: Choose “none of the numerical answers is correct.”
problems.note: The real equation has no roots; applying Vieta without mentioning the number system hides this issue.

problems.title: One root determines the other and a coefficient
problems.question: $x^2-px+45=0$ has root 9. Find the other root plus $p$.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: Root product is 45 and root sum is $p$.
steps: The other root is $45/9=5$. Hence $p=9+5=14$, and the requested sum is $5+14=19$.

problems.title: Factor a parameter fraction
problems.question: Evaluate $(7a+1)/(7a^2-6a-1)$ at $a=\sqrt5+1$.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: Cancel $7a+1$ on the original domain to get $1/(a-1)$. At the given input this is $1/\sqrt5$.

problems.title: Difference between two rational-equation roots
problems.question: Find the absolute difference of roots of $10/(x^2-4x-5)+x/(x+1)=3/(x-5)$.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: Multiply through by the factored denominator: $10+x(x-5)=3(x+1)$.
This gives $x^2-8x+7=(x-1)(x-7)=0$. Both roots are allowed, and their difference is 6.

problems.title: Integer coefficients from rational roots
problems.question: An integer-coefficient quadratic has roots $-0.3,0.5$. Which listed value can its coefficient sum have?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: The displayed primitive integer-coefficient polynomial has the required roots, and coefficient sum $20-4-3=13$.
Every integer-coefficient quadratic with these roots is an integer multiple of this primitive polynomial. Of the listed positive numbers, only 13 is a multiple of 13.

problems.title: Count real roots of a biquadratic
problems.question: How many real solutions does $x^4+5x^2-18=0$ have?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: Then $t^2+5t-18=0$, with roots $(-5\pm\sqrt{97})/2$. Exactly one is positive.
That positive $t$ gives two opposite real $x$ values; the negative $t$ gives none.

problems.title: Coefficient sums depend on normalization
problems.question: A quadratic’s roots are reciprocal and sum to 7. Which listed coefficient sum can occur?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: Root product is 1, so every such equation is $A(x^2-7x+1)=0$, $A\ne0$.
steps: The coefficient sum is $A-7A+A=-5A$. Without a stated leading coefficient or coefficient restriction, it can be any nonzero real number.
Every listed value $5,7,9,-3,-5,-7$ can occur by choosing $A$ accordingly. If the intended equation is monic, its coefficient sum is $-5$.
problems.answer: All six listed values are possible as written; −5 if monic.
problems.note: The source does not specify a monic equation. Multiplying an equation by a nonzero constant preserves its roots and changes its coefficient sum.

problems.title: Roots with a known separation
problems.question: $x^2-10x+c=0$ has roots differing by 8. Find the product of the two roots and $c$.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: Root sum is 10 and product is $c$.
steps: Solve $u+v=10,v-u=8$ to get $u=1,v=9$. Thus $c=9$.
The product $uvc=1\cdot9\cdot9=81$.

problems.title: A square root still imposes a domain
problems.question: Solve $x^2-8(\sqrt x)^2-9=0$.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: Factor $x^2-8x-9=(x-9)(x+1)$. The roots are 9 and $-1$, but the latter is outside the domain.

problems.title: A repeated quadratic expression
problems.question: Find the product of natural solutions of $(3x^2-9x)/2-6/(x^2-3x)=0$.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: The equation becomes $3t/2-6/t=0$, so $t^2=4$.
For $t=-2$, $(x-1)(x-2)=0$, giving natural roots 1,2. For $t=2$, $x=(3\pm\sqrt{17})/2$, neither natural.
The requested product is $1\cdot2=2$.

problems.title: Lake travel followed by downstream travel
problems.question: In one hour a boat travels 16 km on a lake and 18 km down a river flowing out of it. Current speed is 4 km/h. Find the still-water speed.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: Time is distance divided by speed: $16/v+18/(v+4)=1$.
steps: The roots are 32 and $-2$. A speed is positive, so $v=32$.

problems.title: An alloy concentration statement needs a convention
problems.question: An alloy contains 10 kg zinc. Adding 20 kg zinc reduces the copper content “by 25%.” The original mass is at least 30 kg. Find it.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: If original mass is $M$, copper fractions before and after are $(M-10)/M$ and $(M-10)/(M+20)$.
steps: Interpreting the reduction as 25 percentage points gives $20(M-10)/[M(M+20)]=1/4$. This reduces to $M^2-60M+800=0$, with roots 20 and 40.
The condition $M\ge30$ selects 40 kg. If the wording instead means a relative 25% reduction, $M/(M+20)=3/4$ gives 60 kg.
problems.answer: 40 kg under the intended percentage-point reading; 60 kg for a relative reduction.
problems.note: The source says “25%” rather than “25 percentage points.” Its choices indicate the percentage-point interpretation, so both readings are explained.

problems.title: Minimum squared sum of quadratic roots
problems.question: Find the minimum possible sum of squared roots of $x^2-ax+a-3=0$.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: The squared sum is $a^2-2a+6=(a-1)^2+5\ge5$.
The roots are real for every $a$, since the discriminant is $(a-2)^2+8>0$. Equality is attainable at $a=1$.

problems.title: A radical fraction simplifies before substitution
problems.question: Evaluate $[(a+1)/\sqrt a+1/(a-\sqrt a)-a/(\sqrt a+1)](1-a)/(1+a)+2a$ at $a=2$.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: Multiplication by $(1-a)/(1+a)$ gives $-1$. Thus the whole expression is $2a-1$, equal to 3 at $a=2$.

problems.title: Roots in a three-to-seven ratio
problems.question: Roots of $x^2-20x+q=0$ have ratio $3:7$. Find $q$.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: The root sum is 20 and product is $q$.
steps: Write roots $3t,7t$. Then $10t=20$, so $t=2$ and the roots are 6,14.
Their product is $q=84$.

problems.title: Complementary acute-angle functions
problems.question: One acute angle $\alpha$ in a right triangle has $\sin\alpha=\sqrt3/3$. Find the product of sine and tangent of the other acute angle.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: The product is $\cos^2\alpha/\sin\alpha=(1-1/3)/(1/\sqrt3)=2/\sqrt3$.

problems.title: A circle with the altitude as diameter
problems.question: In a right triangle, a circle whose diameter is the altitude from the right vertex cuts lengths 18 and 12 from the legs. Find the leg sum.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: A circle with diameter from $(0,0)$ to $H=(u,v)$ has equation $x^2+y^2-ux-vy=0$.
steps: Put the legs on the coordinate axes. Their second circle intersections are $(u,0),(0,v)$, so $H=(18,12)$ in some order.
The hypotenuse is perpendicular to the altitude vector, hence has equation $18x+12y=18^2+12^2=468$. Its axis intercepts are 26 and 39.
These intercepts are the leg lengths, whose sum is 65.

problems.title: Exact trigonometric values
problems.question: Evaluate $3\tan^230^\circ+4\tan45^\circ+\cos30^\circ\cot30^\circ$.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: The three terms are $1,4,3/2$. Their sum is $13/2=6.5$.

problems.title: An altitude splits a triangle into right triangles
problems.question: Altitude $AD$ splits $BC$ into $BD=2\sqrt2,CD=5$, and $B=60^\circ$. Find $AC$.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: $AD=2\sqrt2\sqrt3=2\sqrt6$. Hence $AC=\sqrt{24+25}=7$.

problems.title: An obtuse isosceles triangle
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has apex angle $120^\circ$ and altitude $3\sqrt3$ to its base. Find the perimeter.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: The altitude bisects the apex and base; $l=h/\cos60^\circ$, $b/2=h\tan60^\circ$.
steps: Each equal side is $6\sqrt3$. The base is $2(3\sqrt3)(\sqrt3)=18$.
The perimeter is $18+12\sqrt3$.

problems.title: Cosine between a median and altitude
problems.question: A right triangle has legs 30,40. Find the cosine of the angle between the median and altitude from its right vertex.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: The direction vectors can be chosen $(a,b)$ and $(b,a)$; $\cos\theta=(u\cdot v)/(|u||v|)$.
steps: The dot product is $2ab$ and the length product $a^2+b^2$.

problems.title: Altitude in a thirty-thirty-one-twenty triangle
problems.question: $AB=BC$, base $AC$, $A=30^\circ$. Altitude $CD$ to line $AB$ has $AD=20$. Find the altitude from $B$ to $AC$.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
steps: $AC=40/\sqrt3$. Thus $AB=AC/\sqrt3=40/3$.
The requested altitude is $AB\sin30^\circ=(40/3)/2=20/3$.

problems.title: A parallelogram diagonal perpendicular to a side
problems.question: A parallelogram has a diagonal of length 3 perpendicular to a side and one angle $30^\circ$. Find the product of adjacent side lengths.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: The diagonal and that side form a right triangle with the other side as hypotenuse; thirty-sixty side ratio $1:\sqrt3:2$.
steps: The diagonal is opposite the $30^\circ$ angle, so it is the short leg 3. The parallelogram sides are $3\sqrt3$ and 6.
The product is $18\sqrt3$.

problems.title: Power of an interior point
problems.question: A point $E$ divides a chord into 15 and 16. Its distance from the circle centre is 4. Find the radius.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.

problems.title: Perpendicular diagonals in a right trapezoid
problems.question: The perpendicular diagonals of a right trapezoid intersect so the longer one is split into lengths 4,9. Find the shorter diagonal.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant identity or geometric relation and keep all restrictions.
formulas: Intersection segments have the base ratio; for a right trapezoid with perpendicular diagonals, $h^2=ab$ and $d_a^2=a(a+b)$.
steps: The bases have ratio $4:9$. The squared diagonal ratio equals the base ratio, hence the diagonal ratio is $2:3$.
The longer diagonal is $4+9=13$. Therefore the shorter is $(2/3)13=26/3$.
